_comment: Keyword lists for Moon-C's intent router. Edit freely: no code changes needed (restart the backend to reload).
_matching: Text and keywords are normalized the same way before matching: lowercase, accents removed, apostrophes removed (can't -> cant), other punctuation replaced by spaces. A keyword matches only as whole words. Categories are checked in strict order: emergency, health, ambiguous, small_talk, then fallback. Keywords of every language are checked for every category, so emergency phrases always work in all four languages (es, en, ru, de) regardless of the active language. Russian and German normalization (same function in Backend/app/intent.py and front-end/src/lib/assistant.js): casefold (German sharp s -> ss), NFKD, combining marks removed, so a/o/u with umlaut -> a/o/u, e with diaeresis -> e and the Russian short i -> i (й -> и). Write keywords naturally (with umlauts or accents) or in these folded forms; typed transliterations (ae, oe, ue) are not folded, add them as extra keywords where they matter.

weak._comment: Plausible but ambiguous phrases (idioms, typos): Moon-C asks a safety question first; only a yes opens the protocol.

stems._comment: Word beginnings. Weak: they only trigger the safety question, never the protocol directly.

de: es fällt mir schwer zu atmen
ich kann die blutung nicht stoppen

emotional_crisis._comment: Thoughts of self-harm or suicide. Always an emergency, checked before every other category; negation is never applied here (the safe side: negatable=false).
de: ich will nicht mehr am leben sein
ich habe keine lust mehr zu leben
es hat keinen sinn mehr zu leben
ich will nicht mehr da sein
ich halte es nicht mehr aus

general_emergency._comment: Used only when no specific emergency protocol matches.

mood._comment: Questions about the mood indicator itself. Feelings (sad, stressed, lonely...) are support moments, see 'support'.

support._comment: Key mental-health moments. Checked after emergency and symptoms, before indicators. Moon-C answers them from shared/support.json, personalized with the crew member's private support profile when there is one.

de: ich halte das nicht mehr aus

wound._comment: A possible injury (cut, wound, scrape, burn). Not an emergency by itself: Moon-C asks how bad it is. 'phrases' match whole words; 'stems' match the start of a word (cortad -> cortada, cortadura), so spelling variants are covered.

exclude._comment: Idioms removed from the text before looking for wound stems (golpe de suerte is luck, burned out is stress).
de: mir ist ein stein vom herzen gefallen

kinds._comment: Which follow-up question an injury gets. Word beginnings matched in order: the first kind with a hit wins (cut = ask about bleeding). Clinical wording lives in Backend/app/chat.py (supuesto: validar con experto medico).

wound_minor._comment: Answers to the wound question that say it is minor. Must not contain 'sangr'/'bleed' words (those open the bleeding protocol).

negation._comment: Negation of an emergency phrase (no sangra, i dont have chest pain). A negator counts when it is at most 3 words before the phrase, only 'fillers' sit between them and no comma/period separates them. A phrase that contains a negator or an 'exempt' word itself (no puedo respirar, cant breathe) is the symptom and is never negated. Moon-C then asks for confirmation instead of opening the protocol.

pain_question._comment: Pain or discomfort in the chest, or breathing trouble, WITHOUT an exact emergency phrase: Moon-C asks first (is it strong?) instead of falling to a generic reply. Fires when the message has a 'where' word start AND a 'feel' word start (or an exact 'feel_words' word).

safety_help._comment: A bare call for help (at most 4 words) with no context: Moon-C asks whether the person is in danger before anything else.

emergency_exact._comment: Messages that are only an emergency number (the whole message, at most the number itself): always a general emergency. A bare number inside a sentence (my pulse is 112) is not one. Mirror in front-end/src/lib/assistant.js.

help._comment: Asking what Moon-C can do (at most 4 words): Moon-C lists its capabilities with buttons.

ack._comment: Short acknowledgements (at most 3 words). Laughter (jajaja, haha) and emoji-only messages are handled in code.

followup._comment: Answers to the safety, pain and injury questions Moon-C asks. 'yes' and 'no' are first words; 'heavy' and 'light' are word beginnings for graded answers (poco, no mucho, bastante); a negation before a heavy word flips it (no es grave = light). Nothing here may open a protocol by itself.

unsure._comment: Phrases at the start of an answer that mean "I do not know": they are not a "no" (no se, не знаю, weiß nicht).

ru: не могу понять что со мной
de: mir geht es nicht so gut
ich weiß nicht was mit mir los ist
ich weiss nicht was mit mir los ist
weiß nicht was mit mir los ist
ich fühle mich nicht wie ich selbst

post_filter_block._comment: Labels the local AI must never use (Moon-C does not diagnose). An AI reply containing any of them is discarded.

post_filter_allow._comment: Everyday pleasantries removed from an AI reply before it is checked for health or emergency keywords, so 'Good night, sleep well!' is not discarded.

crew_query._comment: Questions about a crew member (answered only from alerts, never from chat or profiles). Folded text: lowercase, no accents. Used by app/crewdata.py.

de: wie sieht es bei mir aus

reading._comment: A crew member reports a reading in the chat (number plus indicator). Folded text. Used by app/crewdata.py.

wellbeing._comment: Phrases that open Moon-C's wellbeing flows (backend app/wellbeing.py): acute anxiety (fast guided response), breathing and grounding requests, low mood tips, alerts to the medical officer. Texts live in support_advice.json (supuesto: validar con profesional).
